column3: According to Google's AIP-158, RPCs that return collections must provide pagination at the outset, because adding pagination to an existing method is a backwards-incompatible change.
Request messages for collections should define an `int32` `page_size` field that is not required.
If the user does not specify `page_size` or specifies 0, the API chooses a default, which it should document, and must not return an error.
If the user specifies a `page_size` above the maximum, the API should coerce it down to the maximum, and for a negative value the API must send an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` error.
According to the same AIP, request messages for collections should also define a string `page_token` field that is not required.
The user is expected to keep all other arguments the same when advancing, and if any argument differs the API should send an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` error.
Response messages should define a string `next_page_token` field, which must be empty when the end of the collection has been reached.
The AIP calls that the only way to communicate end-of-collection to users.
According to the same AIP, a paginated request may define an `int32` `skip` field, and its value refers to the number of individual resources to skip, not the number of pages.
A request with no page token and a `skip` of 30 returns a single page starting with the 31st result.
If a `skip` cannot be fulfilled, for example because of the latency of querying a massive data set, the response must be `200 OK` with an empty result set.

According to the Standard Webhooks specification, the most common way to verify the authenticity of webhooks is an HMAC signature with a pre-shared secret key, and a common alternative is an asymmetric signature.
The specification signs the message ID, the timestamp and the body, concatenated and delimited by full-stops as `msg_id.timestamp.payload`.
It sends them in the `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` headers.
The signature header is a space-delimited list so that secrets can be rotated with zero downtime.

According to the same specification, a consumer verifying a symmetric signature should compare it in constant time, should check that `webhook-timestamp` is within some tolerance of the current time to prevent replay attacks, and should use `webhook-id` as an idempotency key so that the same webhook is not processed twice.
According to the same specification, the producer retries a failed delivery until a successful attempt or until delivery appears impossible.
It recommends a retry schedule spanning multiple days with an exponential backoff and some random jitter.
A delivery is successful when the response has a `2xx` status code, and a `410 Gone` response tells the sender to disable the endpoint.
The specification recommends a request timeout between 15 and 30 seconds.

According to the OpenAPI Initiative, in the code-first approach the API is implemented first and its description is created from the code, while in the design-first approach the API description is written first and the code follows.
The OpenAPI Initiative says that, in its opinion, the importance of design-first cannot be stressed strongly enough.
Its reason is that more APIs can be created in code than OpenAPI can describe, so an API built first in code may have to be changed, or its description twisted, to fit what OpenAPI can express.
